symptom: `mxcli diff-local` counted a domain model as modified after `grant read *, write * on entity Shop.Customer to Shop.User` (or any grant/revoke on an entity) and printed no difference — `describe entity` showed the new rule
cause: domainModelBsonToMDL printed each entity's attributes (from the raw map) and the associations, but never the entity's AccessRules, so an access-only change rendered identically at both revisions
insight: diff-local's domain-model renderer reads the raw BSON map, while DESCRIBE ENTITY's grant writer takes the semantic `*domainmodel.Entity` — the temptation is a third grant renderer over the raw map. Instead parse the historical document through the backend (`Parse…FromRaw`, the same gen→semantic conversion GetDomainModel uses) and call the describer's writer, then pin it with a test that every `grant` line `describe entity` prints appears verbatim on diff-local's new side (a where-clause and member lists included). With the class-level note from ako/mxcli#1512 in place, the reverted renderer degrades to `Modified: DomainModel M: changed in properties the MDL rendering does not show: Entities[Item].AccessRules[0]…` rather than silence — which is how to tell the note is working: revert a renderer and the change must still be named
